text:
ashley: Heads-up — seeing ~1.1-1.4GB extra GPU memory per device on multi-GPU inference runs compared to single-GPU. Repro case: tensor-parallel 2, batch=8, seq=2048. Suspect NCCL comm buffers + transient TP shard temps + allocator fragmentation. Attaching quick profile summary below.

dan: Can you paste the specific mem stats / range? nvprof/nsys output? :eyes:

ashley: Quick grab from nsys timeline + runtime logs:
```
GPU0 total 40.0 GB, used before run 3.2 GB, peak during run 18.9 GB
GPU1 total 40.0 GB, used before run 3.1 GB, peak during run 19.6 GB
Observed steady ~1.25 GB extra/resident per GPU vs single-gpu (18.9 vs 17.6).
nvtx shows big allocate/dealloc spikes on kernel switch + ncclCollectives around model-parallel reduceScatter.
Allocator: native cudaMallocAsync enabled; mempool arenas show many small freed blocks not reused across ranks.
Workspace requests spike when selecting fused attention kernel (w/ optimized kernels list v3).
```

kevin: Interesting. Two likely contributors: (1) NCCL temp comm buffers for reduceScatter/allreduce which can allocate workspace equal to shard size, and (2) kernel workspace for the new fused-attn kernels. Also cudaMallocAsync mempool fragmentation can make freed blocks unavailable across concurrent streams.

li: Also check KV cache prefetch concurrency. If we prefetch KV pages for multiple sequences in parallel, each GPU might allocate per-request staging buffers. Did you run with kv_prefetch=on?

ashley: Yes kv_prefetch=on in the repro. Turning it off drops the extra per-GPU by ~400MB in a quick run. So breakdown (approx): NCCL comm temp ~500MB, fused kernel workspace delta ~350MB, kv prefetch staging ~400MB. Fuzziness +/-100MB.

dan: That aligns with an earlier regression we saw after kernel-selection change in release X. Kernel v3 picks a fused-attn that uses an extra workspace buffer for tiled matmuls. When we switched selection to prefer v2 for long sequences memory went down. Do we have telemetry showing kernel selection by seq length?

ashley: Perf traces show runtime picks v3 for seq>=1024 by default. But the heuristics didn't account for TP shard size, so on TP=2 the workspace blowup is proportionally larger.

kevin: Mitigation options:
- Short term: force kernel selection fallback for seq > X or when TP>1 (config toggle).
- Medium: reserve a shared communication buffer pool for NCCL comms that is reused across collectives (avoid repeated cudaMallocs).
- Long term: use CUDA mempool APIs more aggressively (cudaMemPoolCreate, set releaseThreshold) or tune cudaMallocAsync arena sizes to avoid fragmentation.

li: Also consider capping kv_prefetch concurrency and reusing per-GPU staging buffers across requests. A simple global ring buffer per-GPU saved us in a previous test.

ashley: Quick experiment notes I ran:
- disable kv_prefetch -> -400MB
- force kernel=v2 on long seq -> -320MB
- prealloc comm pool (one-time cudaMalloc of 1GB split on first init) -> -460MB (less alloc churn but higher base reserve)
- cudaMallocAsync mempool tuned with arena=4GB -> reduced fragmentation, net -200MB but increased peak allocation latency slightly.

perf-bot: perf/regression: memory-overhead/2024-11-02: baseline 17.5GB -> multi-gpu build 19.0GB (+1.5GB). CC @eng-runtime.

dan: Good data. Action items:
1) Ashley: capture full nsys capture (timeline + memstats) and upload to perf bucket.
2) Kevin: prototype shared NCCL comm buffer pool in the runtime (config flag enable_comm_pool=true). Try reusing buffer across iterations instead of malloc/free per-collective.
3) Li: add a guard in KV prefetch to limit concurrency (max_prefetch_inflight=2) and reuse a per-GPU staging buffer.
4) Runtime team: add heuristic to kernel selector: if tensor-parallel >1, avoid kernels with workspace/alloc > threshold.

ashley: I'll upload traces and a short repro script to the perf bucket by EOD. For the prototyping notes — Kevin, I can share the memory breakdown table I used.

kevin: I'll start a branch for comm-pool. Quick note: make pool optional since some customers prefer zero reserved base. We'll implement on-demand grow but reuse freed chunks.

li: I'll prepare a small test that toggles kv_prefetch concurrency across 0..8 and records per-GPU resident. Will post results tomorrow morning.

ashley: Thanks folks. If anyone wants the quick repro now ping me and I'll drop the shell script here. :thumbsup:

kevin: pinged — grabbing it now.

perf-bot: note: scheduled follow-up meeting in #eng-runtime for 10/31 11:00 to review mitigations.
